title: Uniform exponential moments for first-exit particles of nondegenerate critical branching random walks with exponential offspring moments
source_title: Time spent in a ball by a critical branching random walk
author: Amine Asselah; Bruno Schapira
difficulty_reason: A BGW exponential-moment bound by itself does not control the number of particles frozen at a spatial boundary, because repeated interior generations and spatial displacement remain coupled. The authors first contract the killed tree in generation blocks, then construct a quadratic spatial martingale linking its occupation to the frozen boundary population and control that martingale with the new killed-occupation estimate. The exit-probability and exponential-expansion steps then give the uniform squared-radius and sharper interior-start assertions, beyond standard BGW and random-walk prerequisites.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.3 for nearest-neighbor symmetric branching random walk in any lattice dimension d>=1, nondegenerate critical offspring distribution with finite exponential moment. All three conclusions1.3–1.5 retained: unconditional first-exit particle exponential moment, conditional-on-nonempty bound, and first-order normalized bound from the half-radius ball. Read complete generation-block contraction Proposition1.4(20–21), the quadratic spatial martingale and exponential compensation21–23, supporting BGW exponential bound9–10 and first/second-moment exit lower bound14. Proposition3.11(15–16) is explicitly attributed to Zhu16a; its full provided proof was also read. Kolmogorov BGW estimates, elementary random-walk exit estimates and cited generating-function boundsAN04 are named prior foundations. Nondegeneracy is essential to the source standing extinction/Kolmogorov setting; no deterministic one-child offspring law included. No exterior-start/dimension-four logarithmic tail or full occupation tail theorem claimed reviewed or counted. PDF authorsAmine Asselah andBruno Schapira,11/2024/281/license verified.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors control a killed tree through generation-block contraction, couple its occupation to frozen boundary particles by a quadratic spatial martingale, and obtain uniform exponential moments at the natural squared-radius scale. This spatial branching estimate exceeds qualifying-exam martingale techniques.
